Joint Model of Recurrent Readmission and Death (Draft)

Source: R/joint_readmission_death.R
joint_readmission_death.Rd

Fits readmission and death together instead of treating death as censoring of the readmission process. Two sub-models are fit on the same counting-process data:

  1. Readmission: an Andersen-Gill recurrent-event Cox model ([recurrent_cox()], `model = "ag"`, or `"frailty"` with `frailty = TRUE`) for the rate of readmissions.

  2. Death: a Cox model for the time to death, with the subject's readmission history as a time-varying covariate (`n_prior_readmissions`, the number of readmissions before the interval), so the death hazard depends on the recurrent process. With `frailty = TRUE` it adds a gamma frailty for the subject.

Usage

joint_readmission_death(
  data,
  readmission_predictors,
  death_predictors,
  id = "id",
  start = "tstart",
  stop = "tstop",
  status = "status",
  death = "death",
  frailty = FALSE,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of counting-process intervals, as for [recurrent_cox()].

readmission_predictors

Covariates of the readmission model: a character vector of column names, or a one-sided formula such as `~ age + sex`. In this draft they must be numeric columns (see `predict()`).

death_predictors

Covariates of the death model: a character vector of column names, or a one-sided formula. In this draft they must be numeric columns (see `predict()`).

id, start, stop, status, death

Column names (strings) of the subject identifier, the interval start and stop, the readmission indicator (0/1), and the death indicator (0/1; see Details).

frailty

Logical (default `FALSE`). With `TRUE`, both sub-models get a gamma frailty for the subject.

conf_level

Confidence level of the hazard ratios (default `0.95`).

Value

An object of class `joint_readmission_death`: a list with `readmission` (the [recurrent_cox()] fit), `death_fit` (the [survival::coxph()] death fit, fitted with `model = TRUE`, so the stored model frame makes it usable with standard generics such as [survival::basehaz()] and [survival::survfit()]), `terms` (a combined tibble with `process`, `term`, `estimate`, `std_error`, `hr`, `conf_low`, `conf_high`, `statistic` and `p_value`), `death_terms` (the death sub-model's terms), `n_subjects`, `n_intervals`, `n_readmissions`, `n_deaths`, `frailty`, `frailty_variance` (named `readmission` and `death`, `NA` unless `frailty = TRUE`), and `conf_level`. `tidy()` returns `terms`.

Details

**Draft status – this departs from the package's standing assumption.** `NEWS.md` 0.8.0 ("Not done, and why") explicitly declined joint models of readmission and death, with the reason that death ends follow-up (censoring), the usual assumption of the Andersen-Gill and PWP models, which is informative when death is common; that is also stated in the help of [recurrent_intervals()]. This function is a draft extension built at the maintainer's request, and it does **not** replace that assumption elsewhere in the package: [recurrent_cox()], [cv_coxnet()] and the other recurrent tools still treat death as censoring.

**What the draft does and does not do.** The two processes are linked by the `n_prior_readmissions` covariate in the death model, not by a single shared frailty estimated jointly: with `frailty = TRUE` each sub-model gets its own gamma frailty (one for readmissions, one for death), and the two frailty variances are reported separately. A fully joint likelihood with one shared frailty (as in `frailtypack::frailtyPenal()`) is follow-up work and is not implemented here; it would also add a dependency the package does not currently have. Death-survival predictions are conditional on a fixed number of prior readmissions (see `predict()`): they do not integrate over the readmission process.

**Death in the data.** `death` marks the subject's death at the stop time of an interval: `1` on the subject's last interval when they died there, `0` elsewhere. A subject who is readmitted and later dies gets a final interval ending at death (`status = 0`, `death = 1`); a row must not carry both a readmission and a death, and no rows may follow a death. Subjects who do not die are censored for death at the end of follow-up.

**Frailty with competing risks.** With `frailty = TRUE`, this is also the draft's frailty-with-competing-risks support: the readmission and death processes – which compete, in that death ends the readmission process – each carry a subject frailty. As above, the frailties are fitted separately per process, not shared; a shared frailty across the competing processes is follow-up work.

See also

[recurrent_cox()], [recurrent_intervals()], [joint_model()], [cv_coxnet()]

Examples

if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  n <- 150
  subj <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n), age = rnorm(n), end = 120)
  ev <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    k <- rpois(1, exp(0.3 * subj$age[i]) * 1.2)
    if (k == 0) return(NULL)
    data.frame(id = i, time = sort(runif(k, 1, 120)))
  }))
  long <- recurrent_intervals(ev, subj)
  long$age <- subj$age[long$id]
  # Deaths: about a quarter of subjects, at the end of follow-up
  long$death <- 0L
  died <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 + 0.5 * subj$age))
  for (i in which(died == 1)) {
    idx <- which(long$id == i)
    long$death[idx[length(idx)]] <- 1L
  }
  fit <- joint_readmission_death(long, ~ age, ~ age)
  fit
  generics::tidy(fit)
}
